ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder

s1.syndrome_frame: febrile urinary tract infection with possible obstructive uropathy and concern for malignancy in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Escherichia coli growth in blood and urine cultures
irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall on CT
key_facts: history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
immunosuppressive therapy with prednisone and tacrolimus
prophylactic antimicrobial therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, itraconazole, and valganciclovir
urinalysis positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells
blood and urine cultures grow Escherichia coli
CT of abdomen and pelvis shows non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis and irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall on CT, suspicious for neoplasm

shortlist.label: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
shortlist.why_kept: immunosuppressive therapy and history of transplantation increase risk

shortlist.label: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: foul-smelling urine and leukocytosis suggest severe urinary tract infection

shortlist.label: Emphysematous cystitis
shortlist.why_kept: diabetes is not mentioned, but foul-smelling urine and leukocytosis suggest severe infection

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: less common than urothelial carcinoma, but possible given symptoms and CT findings

raw.rationale: The CT of the abdomen and pelvis reveals irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall, which is suspicious for neoplasm, and given the patient's 70-pack-year smoking history, which is a significant risk factor for urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
rejected.why: While the patient is immunosuppressed, the imaging findings and clinical presentation are more suggestive of a primary bladder malignancy rather than a lymphoproliferative disorder.

rejected.label: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a more chronic course and is associated with obstructive uropathy, which is not indicated by the non-obstructing nephrolithiasis in this case.

rejected.label: Emphysematous cystitis
rejected.why: This is an acute infection of the bladder characterized by gas in the bladder wall, which is not mentioned in the imaging findings.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
rejected.why: While this is a possible bladder malignancy, the patient's risk factors and the imaging findings are more suggestive of urothelial carcinoma, which is more common in smokers.
